headline: Benchmarks reveal tool-dependent accuracy in nanopore and metagenomic profiling
label: Metagenomic Tool Benchmarking
summary: Benchmarks across read filtering, viral detection, binning, 16S classification and strain profiling show tool choice governs accuracy in microbial genomics.
synthesis: The common thread is benchmarking of analysis tools for bacterial and metagenomic data against simulated or controlled ground truth. Trimming and quality-filtering pipelines for Nanopore bacterial reads were scored on SNP F1 and assembly quality across 13 isolates, with Filtlong ranking highest on SNP F1. Eleven viral prediction tools were tested on low-abundance metagenomes, and two-tool combinations with Kraken2X filtering improved viral recovery. DeepMM splits chimeric contigs before binning, reducing reference-discordant gene annotations and virulence calls in near-complete MAGs. For marker-based profiling, updated 16S databases such as GreenGenes2 and full-length long-read sequencing affect species-level resolution, while nanopore rRNA operon sequencing, with error rates below ~0.008 errors/base, supports strain-level quantification. In simulated mixed-strain E. coli metagenomes, gene content recovers well whereas MLST and serotypes do not. What is new is the emphasis on how tool choice limits resolution at strain and species levels.
